picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: colored copy (German edition) of the 1572 plate, trimmed to the ‘Parma’ panel of the four-city sheet; walled town on both banks with the cathedral and baptistery

picks.what: View across the Ducal Park to the city, watercolor (Museo Glauco Lombardi)
picks.why: color general view with the skyline of domes and towers behind the park

picks.file: Panorama di Parma, visto dall’Osservatorio Astronomico (xilografia).jpg
picks.what: Panorama from the observatory, wood engraving in Le Cento Città d’Italia
picks.why: rooftop panorama with the Steccata dome, cathedral and baptistery

gaps: P0: no candidates; P2: nothing usable; P6: no modern photograph among the candidates
notes: #19 is a loose, painterly view; drop it if a documentary picture is preferred for P5. P1 alternatives: #7 is the same Parma panel colored but only 1004 px; #1 is the earlier anonymous print (about 1570) that Braun and Hogenberg copied, uncolored and small. Skipped #2/#3 (Siege of Neuss by the Duke of Parma), #4/#5 (other copies of the same B&H sheet), #8 (1639 town plan), #9 (Bellotto capriccio of Rome held in Parma), #10 (1726 small generic view in Les Forces de l’Europe), #15 (Paris interior), #16 (1840 SDUK map; the panorama is only a thin inset strip). P3 alternatives: #11/#13 (Palazzo Ducale and Pilotta, about 1835/1840) and #14 (Piazza Maggiore, 1845) are single-square scenes, too close in date to #12 for a second P3.
